precepts.text: But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners, right?
precepts.point: But listen, then you pray to God. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners, right? So it say above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a friend, you go to God and he's going to direct your path. Look what it says next.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
“But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord.” Your everyday life should generally be spent around godly people. We have to go out in the world and work, but outside of that, the bulk of your time is with godly men, and if the brothers around you don't have understanding, be around people with more understanding than you so you can level up. How will you know he keeps the commandments? You have to be exercised to discern between good and evil. If you are keeping the commandments, you'll be around godly men, because every beast consorteth with its own kind.

He is one whose mind is according to thy mind, “and will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry”: he's going to correct you. So how is your mind? It has to be godly. When it says “let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it”, that is not for the man who isn't seeking counsel, who is watching porn, whatever he's doing, and then making decisions. You're going to make a mistake. In a multitude of counsel there is safety; the counsel of your own heart stands when it's funneled through the laws of God. “For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower”: the seven watchmen are godly men, and your own godly mind can see what's best for you.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” Above the counsel of your own heart, above the counsel of a godly man, you go to God, and he directs your path. But God is not going to hear the prayer of sinners: “If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me.” Your prayer for direction is only heard if your heart is not holding on to iniquity.

“Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” So it's not telling you not to get counsel from brothers. Get counsel, balance it with what you think might be right, with a godly mind, and then go to God and ask him to direct your path.

precepts.text: Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men, heathen and wicked Israelite alike.
precepts.point: The people lamented and said, Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God? So they sent messengers to Kirjath-jearim to come fetch the ark up. The Bible acknowledges the Most High God as the king of terrors: he was killing thousands at a time, and his judgments are terrifying.

note.label: 1 Samuel 6: The Ark Returned with a Trespass Offering

precepts.why:
“Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men.” The children of men here is everybody: heathen and wicked Israelite alike.

The Philistines were smitten for taking the ark, and now the men of Beth-shemesh, Israelites, were smitten for looking into it: “the Lord had smitten many of the people with a great slaughter.” He is terrible in his doing, and being an Israelite did not spare the ones who went where the Lord gave them no authority to go.

So the people lamented and said, “Who is able to stand before this holy Lord God?” That is the right question. Come and see his works, and learn to fear him.

precepts.text: If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me; somewhere in the camp there was iniquity, so the Lord did not hear Saul.
precepts.point: If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason.

note.label: 1 Samuel 14: By Many or by Few

precepts.why:
Saul proposed, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light”, and the people agreed. Then the priest said, “Let us draw near hither unto God.” Saul asked, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.”

“If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me”. Somewhere in the camp there was iniquity, so the Lord did not hear Saul. If you are spiritual, when the Lord ignores you, you understand at that point what it reveals: it is sin. It has to be; the scriptures give only that reason.

points: Make a joyful noise unto the Most High, all lands; sing forth the honor of His name and make His praise glorious.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: Say unto the Most High how terrible He is in His works; through the greatness of His power His enemies submit themselves, and all the earth shall worship and sing unto Him.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: Come and see the works of the Most High, terrible in His doing toward the children of men, who turned the sea into dry land so they went through the flood on foot.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: He rules by His power forever; His eyes behold the nations, and let not the rebellious exalt themselves.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: Bless the Most High and make the voice of His praise heard, who holds the soul in life and does not suffer the feet to be moved.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: He proved and tried His people as silver is tried, brought them into the net, laid affliction upon their loins, and caused men to ride over their heads, but brought them out through fire and water into a wealthy place.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: David will go into the house of the Most High with burnt offerings and pay the vows his lips uttered and his mouth spoke when he was in trouble.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: He will offer burnt sacrifices of fatlings with the incense of rams, and offer bullocks with goats.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: Come and hear, all that fear the Most High, and he will declare what He has done for his soul; he cried unto Him with his mouth and He was extolled with his tongue.

note.label: Psalm 66: Come and See the Works of God

points: If he regarded iniquity in his heart the Most High would not hear him, but truly He heard and attended to the voice of his prayer; blessed be the Most High, who has not turned away his prayer nor His mercy from him.
